Figure 1:Teaser.L3G-Worldgenerates an explorable, spatially consistent world in real time from a single image and a camera trajectory.
To this end, L3G-Mem maintains a latent 3D Gaussian memory, and L3G-Gen generates video conditioned on VAE latents rendered from the memory.

Figure 2:L3G-Mem.(a) L3G-Mem takes the current window𝒲k\mathcal{W}_{k}and the memoryℳk−1\mathcal{M}_{k-1}. Renderingℳk−1\mathcal{M}_{k-1}into the current cameras determines which geometry features are clustered by K-means into spawning queries, and identifies the visible Gaussians whose memory tokens are retrieved as refinement tokens. Both token sets are jointly processed by a transformer and decoded into new Gaussians and residual updates, respectively.
(b) Given the input video chunk, RGB and opacity rendered from the previous memory identify regions requiring new Gaussians through a spawning mask. As a result, the updated memory can fully reconstruct the observed scene.

Figure 3:L3G-Gen.(a) L3G-Gen renders the VAE latents and opacity of the 3D memory to the target cameras, concatenates them with the noisy latents along the channel dimension, and generates the next chunk conditioned on the history latents.
(b) We visualize the ground-truth and generated video, with target-view rendered VAE condition from the latent 3D Gaussian memory, illustrating that spatially aligned latent memory provides consistent conditioning for video generation.

Figure 4:L3G-World Pipeline.L3G-World couples video generation and memory updating in a chunk-wise loop, where each generated chunk updates the persistent 3D memory, which in turn conditions subsequent chunk generation.

Figure 5:Qualitative results of L3G-World.(a) L3G-Mem corrects geometric errors in the 3D memory through residual refinement using video chunks generated by L3G-Gen.
(b) L3G-World maintains scene consistency over long-horizon generation through its persistent 3D memory.
(c) Rendering the memory’s VAE features from target camera views provides spatially aligned conditioning, enabling consistent video generation along diverse camera trajectories.

Figure 6:Qualitative results of video generation on DL3DV and RealEstate10K.For each scene, all methods start from the same input view (top), explore unseen regions (middle), and return to the initial camera location (bottom). L3G-World preserves scene structure and appearance upon loop closure, whereas the baselines exhibit drift, blur, or rendering artifacts.
Figure 7:Qualitative results of ablation study of L3G-World on DL3DV.Memory refinement can not fix geometric error in 3D memory, leading blurry video due to memory rendering artifacts.

Figure 8:Additional qualitative results of video generation on DL3DV and RealEstate10K.For each scene, all methods start from the same input view (top), explore unseen regions (middle), and return to the initial camera location (bottom). L3G-World preserves scene structure and appearance upon loop closure, whereas the baselines exhibit drift, blur, or rendering artifacts.

Figure 9:Visualization of latent 3D Gaussian memory conditioning for video generation.We visualize the ground-truth and generated video, with target-view rendered VAE condition from the latent 3D Gaussian memory, illustrating that spatially aligned latent memory provides consistent conditioning for video generation.
